subject: Renewal amendment: dedicated capacity scale-up and revised reserved pricing
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@brightscale.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom@brightscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal amendment: proposal to scale dedicated pool to 32 GPUs

Hi Elena / Tom,

As we approach your renewal window (July 1), I put together a proposal to migrate BrightScale's Dedicated reservation from 16→32 GPUs and lock a revised reserved rate that reflects scale. Summary below and attached: BrightScale_Renewal_Quote_20260612.pdf (PDF, 1 page).

Summary (12‑month term, reserve pool: BS-DED-16 → BS-DED-32):
- Current: 16 reserved GPUs at $3.50 / GPU‑hour (effective) → baseline $56.00 / hour.
- Proposed: 32 reserved GPUs at $2.90 / GPU‑hour (committed reserved rate) → $92.80 / hour.
- Committed throughput SLA: sustained throughput for 32 GPUs, 99th percentile token latency target unchanged.
- Start/term: amendment effective on renewal date (2026‑07‑01) for 12 months.
- Ramp: we can schedule a staged activation (16→24 on day 1, remainder within 72 hours) to avoid downtime.
- One-time account credit: none in base proposal; open to limited promotional credit tied to signature timeline.

Why this helps BrightScale: lower per‑GPU unit economics as you scale; simplified capacity headroom for peaks; reserved pool isolation for compliance.

If you want, I can share a 6‑month stepped pricing alternative (intro discount then standard rate). Would you like me to propose the stepped option or is the above straightforward to circulate for approval?

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555‑0198

Attachment: BrightScale_Renewal_Quote_20260612.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: Elena Morris <elena@brightscale.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@brightscale.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal amendment: proposal to scale dedicated pool to 32 GPUs

Thanks, Sean — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick questions / asks from our side before we can approve:

1) Pricing: $2.90 is a helpful step but our finance team is pushing for $2.60 / GPU‑hour for a 12‑month commit given the volume increase. Can you run that by your team?
2) Burst: can you provide a 10% free burst credit for the first month (we have a big migration test coming up) so we don't hit limits while we validate load?
3) Contract language: we need explicit wording on the throughput guarantee (99th pct latency) and an escalation path if there are sustained violations.

If you can get closer on pricing (or a stepped discount: e.g., $2.60 for first 6 months, $2.90 thereafter) we'll be able to sign quickly.

Elena
Elena Morris
Head of Platform, BrightScale Analytics
elena@brightscale.ai

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding BrightScale's counter. Key asks: $2.60 / GPU‑hour for 12 months OR stepped (2.60 → 2.90), plus 10% free burst credit for month 1; explicit SLA language.

Margins on 32 GPUs at $2.90/hr are already tight but acceptable; $2.60/hr materially reduces gross margin. Attachment: internal_margin_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet) with quick margin calc for both scenarios.

Is there flexibility for a stepped compromise (2.70 for first 6 months then 2.95 thereafter) + 10% burst credit? That preserves some margin while helping close. If you approve, I'll update the amendment and route for signature.

Thanks,
Sean

Attachment: internal_margin_calc.xlsx (XLSX, internal)

Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightScale renewal - customer asking for $2.60/gpu-hr + burst credit (need approval)

Sean — reviewed. Approve the stepped compromise with the following guardrails:

- Offer: $2.70 / GPU‑hour for the first 6 months, then $2.95 / GPU‑hour for the remaining term (12‑month total).
- Grant a one‑time 10% burst credit for month 1 tied to technical validation; credit cannot be banked.
- Add SLA paragraph: 99th percentile token latency target; if sustained SLA failures >3 days, provide service credits (per standard SLA schedule) and escalation to engineering on a 24‑hr response SL.
- Require signature by 2026‑06‑20 to qualify for the stepped pricing.

Sean — proceed to update the amendment PDF and generate DocuSign. Keep me in the loop if they push back further.

Marissa

- Pricing: $2.70 / GPU‑hour for months 1–6; $2.95 / GPU‑hour months 7–12.

DocuSign link: https://na1.docusign.net/DocuSign/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?po=AMND-2026-BS-1127
